key_insight: Better web agents need targeted practice on reusable skills, not just more tasks. MiniWeb makes it possible to identify which interaction skills fail instead of measuring only overall task success.
problem_solved: Task-level success rates can hide why browser agents struggle. Researchers need realistic workflows with skill-level annotations to diagnose weaknesses and guide training.
method: Build MiniWeb: 65 interconnected websites spanning 15 domains for realistic navigation, search, and transactions.
Provide 369 human-annotated tasks labeled with 37 reusable interaction primitives organized into 7 skill families.
Use skill-level evaluation to pinpoint failure patterns; the provided abstract mentions benchmarking ten open-weight models but is truncated before reporting results.
impact: MiniWeb gives practitioners a structured way to diagnose browser-agent weaknesses and prioritize targeted training. Its reusable skill taxonomy could support more informative comparisons than task-success scores alone.
visual_elements: Miniature web map showing 65 connected websites grouped into 15 domains.
Skill hierarchy showing 7 families branching into 37 interaction primitives.
Workflow strip illustrating navigation → search → transaction, with skill labels attached to each step.
Conceptual skill-diagnostic heatmap contrasting overall task success with individual skill failures, without implying reported results.
paper_title: Back to Basics: A Skill-Centric Approach to Generalist Web Agents
paper_authors: Minh Pham-Dinh, Md Farhan Ishmam, Hernan Yupanqui, Reaz Hassan Joarder, Kenneth Marino
